B has stronger semantic examples and a sharper rule for when to add a token ('a second screen or team needs it'). But B says to keep one-offs local as exceptions, then says 'no new one-off values in PRs,' which contradicts itself. Both stay well under 120 words, and both add notes after the message. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both drafts stay under 120 words. A's naming examples are more consistently role-based, and it tells people outright to reuse the nearest token. It also gives a clear test for adding one: a second screen or team needs it. B names approvers and a review cadence, but its `space-4`/`space-8` examples are named by value, which undercuts its 'purpose, not value' rule, and it never tells people to use the closest existing token. B is cleaner to paste because it has no preamble, though both add a note after the message.
